title: Story of the Jews
series: A series of histories, each told from the perspective of a different people. Later books (Book Two: Story of the Arabs, then Story of the Persians) are coming later and not yet written.
perspective: Told from the perspective of Israel and the Jewish people. Other peoples appear as the world around them.
intro: This is the story of the Jewish people, told on a map. It begins with a name carved in stone. Around 1208 BC an Egyptian king listed his enemies in Canaan, and among them was a people called Israel. Jewish tradition remembers this early world through the Torah: the patriarchs, slavery in Egypt, the Exodus and the covenant at Sinai. Ancient inscriptions and archaeology add their own evidence. Here both are told side by side, and every line says whether it is attested, disputed, or tradition.

stops.label: 1207 BC
stops.title: Israel is named
stops.summary: Around 1208 BC Pharaoh Merneptah names a people called Israel on a stone, the oldest known mention of the name. Then the palace world of the Late Bronze Age falls, the Sea Peoples arrive, and new villages spread across the hills of Canaan.

stops.label: c. 1150 BC
stops.title: Villages in the hills
stops.summary: The Philistines hold five cities on the coast while the hill villages of Israel grow. Jewish tradition tells of Shiloh, the Judges and Saul, the first king; the chapter ends with what can and cannot be known about David.

stops.label: c. 1000 BC
stops.title: David and Solomon: tradition and evidence
stops.summary: The Bible tells of David's Jerusalem and Solomon's temple, and archaeologists still debate how large their kingdom was. Tradition and evidence are told side by side, until the kingdom divides into Israel and Judah.

stops.label: c. 930 BC
stops.title: Israel and Judah
stops.summary: Israel and Judah live side by side among Aram, Moab and a rising Assyria. Omri makes Samaria a capital, and stones from Qarqar, Moab, Dan and Nimrud name Israel's kings, down to Jehu's tribute in 841 BC.

stops.label: 722 BC
stops.title: Fall of Samaria
stops.summary: Aram presses on Israel, then Assyria returns to stay. Jeroboam II's Israel prospers and Amos and Hosea speak out, until Tiglath-pileser III takes Galilee and Samaria falls. Its people are carried off, and Judah stands alone.

stops.label: 701 BC
stops.title: Sennacherib at Jerusalem
stops.summary: Coming soon. Sennacherib of Assyria marches on Judah, takes Lachish and shuts Hezekiah up in Jerusalem.

soon.title: Sennacherib at Jerusalem
soon.text: Next chapter coming soon. Samaria has fallen and Israel is an Assyrian province. In 701 BC a new king of Assyria, Sennacherib, marches on Judah. He takes Lachish and shuts Hezekiah up in Jerusalem, 'like a bird in a cage'. That is where the next chapter begins.
